claims.text: The catalyst system is a nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution.
Miscibility is enhanced at the subnanoscale because crystallization-related miscibility limits are largely eliminated.
Enhanced subnanoscale miscibility increases synergy between dissimilar elements.
Synergy between dissimilar elements improves ethanol-oxidation activity in PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts.
The controlled change is the Pt-to-other-element ratio, including introduction or variation of Zr.
The proposed test is conducted under electrochemical ethanol-oxidation conditions.
Subnanoalloy structure and composition govern the strength of synergistic effects.
Heterometallic bonding can alter Pt electronic states and shift its d-band center, thereby influencing catalytic specificity.
A selected subnanoalloy composition will improve ethanol-oxidation activity relative to unary and nanoparticle baselines.
A selected subnanoalloy composition will improve ethanol-oxidation selectivity relative to the baseline.
Pt4Zr2 is an example of the composition expected to provide optimal performance.
The baseline includes unary Pt and Zr subnanoparticles and PtZr nanoparticles.
A linear average of Pt20 and Zr20 exchange currents is an appropriate quantitative baseline.
The hypothesis is limited to particles smaller than 1 nm.
The exact ethanol-oxidation mechanism and the role of each element in PtPdRhRuIrOs are not fully understood.
Scalability of the proposed subnanoalloy behavior to larger particles and more complex reactions is uncertain.
Exchange currents, Tafel slopes, catalytic activity, and selectivity are the proposed experimental measurements.
Failure of the selected composition to improve activity and selectivity would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated target is the six-element PtPdRhRuIrOs system, but the intervention, proposed optimum, and controls shift to a binary Pt-Zr system containing an element absent from the target composition.

The hypothesis concerns ethanol oxidation, whereas the cited exchange-current and Tafel evidence concerns the hydrogen evolution reaction in sulfuric acid; those records do not establish an ethanol-oxidation baseline or selectivity measurement.
